cls: Triazole antifungal (administered as the water-soluble prodrug isavuconazonium sulfate)
quick: Loading 372 mg (=200 mg isavuconazole) q8h x6 doses, then 372 mg once daily
May be taken with or without food; swallow capsules whole
May cause fetal harm; avoid unless benefit outweighs risk
No dose adjustment, including severe impairment and dialysis
No adjustment for mild-moderate; not studied in severe (Child-Pugh C)
Liver tests, ECG/QT, signs of infusion reaction
summary: Isavuconazole (Cresemba) is a broad-spectrum triazole antifungal administered as the prodrug isavuconazonium sulfate, which is hydrolyzed in plasma to active isavuconazole. It is indicated for invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis in adults and in pediatric patients. Treatment begins with a loading regimen every 8 hours for 6 doses (48 hours), then once-daily maintenance. Notable features include hepatotoxicity and a dose-related SHORTENING of the QT interval, making it CONTRAINDICATED in familial short QT syndrome; it is a CYP3A4 substrate and a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, so significant drug interactions are expected.
indications: Invasive aspergillosis in patients 1 year of age and older
Invasive mucormycosis in patients 1 year of age and older

dosage.d: 372 mg isavuconazonium sulfate (equivalent to 200 mg isavuconazole) every 8 hours
dosage.n: Oral = 2 capsules of 186 mg; IV = 1 reconstituted vial; do not divide, crush, or chew capsules
Start maintenance 12 to 24 hours after the last loading dose

dosage.d: Oral and IV are interchangeable at the same isavuconazonium dose
dosage.n: High oral bioavailability (~98%) allows switching without dose change

dosage.d: Loading dose every 8 hours for 6 doses then once-daily maintenance, dose per weight band
dosage.n: Follow current pediatric weight-based dosing in the prescribing information

admin: Swallow capsules whole; do not chew, crush, dissolve, or open
May be administered with or without food
For IV: reconstitute the vial and dilute in 250 mL of a compatible diluent (0.9% sodium chloride or 5% dextrose)
Administer IV over a minimum of 1 hour through an infusion set with an in-line filter (pore size 0.2 to 1.2 micron)
Do not administer as an IV bolus; flush the line with the same diluent before and after infusion
Start once-daily maintenance 12 to 24 hours after the last loading dose
moa: Isavuconazole, the active moiety released from the prodrug isavuconazonium sulfate, inhibits the fungal cytochrome P-450 enzyme lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51), which is required for the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. Depletion of ergosterol and accumulation of methylated sterol precursors disrupts the fungal cell membrane structure and function, inhibiting fungal growth.

absolute: Familial short QT syndrome (isavuconazole shortens the QT interval)
Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, high-dose ritonavir)
Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, St. John's wort, long-acting barbiturates)
relative: Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) - not studied
Pre-existing or risk of hepatic injury
Concomitant CYP3A4 substrates with narrow therapeutic index

preg: Based on animal data, isavuconazole may cause fetal harm (skeletal and other malformations). Avoid use in pregnancy unless the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus; advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment.
lact: It is not known whether isavuconazole is present in human milk; it is excreted in the milk of lactating animals. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment is required for any degree of renal impairment, including severe impairment and end-stage renal disease. The intravenous formulation contains a cyclodextrin excipient (SBECD); however, the prescribing information does not require dose adjustment in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B); use only if benefit outweighs risk in these patients. It has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) and is not recommended in this group. Hepatic adverse reactions, including elevated transaminases, have occurred; monitor liver tests and discontinue if signs of significant liver injury develop.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, high-dose ritonavir) - contraindicated; increase isavuconazole exposure
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, St. John's wort, long-acting barbiturates) - contraindicated; decrease isavuconazole exposure
Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates (e.g., sirolimus, tacrolimus, cyclosporine) - isavuconazole increases their levels; monitor and adjust
moderate: Digoxin (P-gp substrate) - increased digoxin levels; monitor
Mycophenolate mofetil - increased exposure to active metabolite
Other QT-shortening agents - additive QT shortening
Atorvastatin and other CYP3A4-metabolized statins - increased exposure
minor: Mild CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers - modest exposure changes
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food has no clinically meaningful effect on absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol due to additive potential for hepatotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate hepatic transaminases and bilirubin; shortens the QTc interval on ECG (unlike most azoles, which prolong it).

serious: Infusion-related reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, chills, dizziness, paresthesia)
Hypersensitivity and severe skin reactions (e.g., SJS)

monitoring: Liver function tests at baseline and periodically during therapy
ECG/QT interval, particularly in patients at risk of arrhythmia or on other QT-affecting drugs
Signs of infusion-related reactions during IV administration
Signs of hypersensitivity or severe skin reactions
counsel: Swallow capsules whole; do not chew, crush, or open them
Take maintenance doses at the same time each day; may be taken with or without food
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, nausea/vomiting, or abdominal pain (possible liver injury)
Tell your doctor about all medicines and supplements, especially St. John's wort and HIV/TB drugs
Report any history of short QT syndrome or family history of sudden cardiac death
pk: Therapeutic levels achieved during the 48-hour loading regimen
Capsules: store at 20-25 C; IV vials: refrigerate 2-8 C
pearls: Given as the prodrug isavuconazonium sulfate; 372 mg of the salt equals 200 mg of active isavuconazole
Unlike most azoles, isavuconazole SHORTENS the QT interval - it is CONTRAINDICATED in familial short QT syndrome
Loading dose: q8h for 6 doses (48 h), then once daily starting 12-24 h after the last loading dose
CYP3A4 substrate AND moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor - contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers
High oral bioavailability allows seamless oral/IV switching at the same dose without titration
Monitor liver tests; IV formulation does not require dose change in renal impairment
missed: If a maintenance dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular once-daily schedule; do not take a double dose.
overdose: Symptoms reported at higher exposures include headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, paresthesia, palpitations, and QT shortening. There is no specific antidote; manage supportively with cardiac (ECG) and clinical monitoring. Isavuconazole is not significantly removed by hemodialysis.
